placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0077). This building does not stand where a northing in the recipe put it: it stands on the north face of blk_lake_clark, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is set 0.80 m back from that lot line, the alignment the two frontage buildings already standing on this face use, and its east wall is fixed by the west wall of recon_1835_south_d5_016, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, and this placement carries none of the jitter the parcel's interior rows carry, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the plate supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous storefront row on the town's principal street rather than detached cottages set back on grass — and the treatment is what this placement takes from it. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred shoemaker's household (2 of 3 this layer infers): hh_inf_shoemaker_south_02 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

residents.name: The Leland household — a reconstructed shoemaker (south division)
residents.why: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_south_d4_014 is an anonymous reconstructed roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.

persons.name: Asa Leland
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. THE NAME IS INVENTED TOO, and `name_basis` beside it says so and says which pool it came from: this record used to carry a bare designation instead, on the reasoning that a surname would make it look like the documented layer, but a town of designations does not read as a town and the grade, this note and name_basis all say plainly which layer this is. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE SECOND OF 3 SHOEMAKER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER RECONSTRUCTS. Three thousand two hundred and sixty-five people wear out boots in a town whose streets are mud for half the year, and the nearest bench otherwise is Detroit. The schedule allows six W4 small artisan shops; three shoemaking households are inferred, one of them working from an anonymous shop roof already on the plat.

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - second of 3 shoemaker households in this layer, in the south division. Three thousand two hundred and sixty-five people wear out boots in a town whose streets are mud for half the year, and the nearest bench otherwise is Detroit. The schedule allows six W4 small artisan shops; three shoemaking households are inferred, one of them working from an anonymous shop roof already on the plat. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.

frontage.why: T-0077, the owner's ask of 2026-08-18 on the Tremont House street scene: "there should be more and denser buildings. this is important." He sent the plate of this corner — a continuous two-storey storefront row, shoulder to shoulder on shared party lines — beside a screenshot of this same corner in the render, where the Tremont stands alone on open grass. Four of this row's anonymous roofs stood in the Clark-Dearborn block SEVENTEEN TO TWENTY-FOUR METRES behind the Lake Street frontage, each nudged off the line by its own jitter, which is the shape of a distribution and not of a street. They now stand ON the frontage: the line, its bearing and the corner they pack back from are read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and this file authors no coordinate for any of them. The 0.80 m setback is not a measurement — it is the line the two frontage buildings ALREADY standing on this face (inf_bakery_lake and inf_butcher_market) use, adopted so the street wall is one wall rather than three. No roof is added, moved out of its block, renamed or re-dimensioned: the parcel still deals 40 principal and 8 ancillary, and every id and band is the one it was.
